A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STFlow research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and technical appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original STFlow results on N-body systems, MD17 molecular trajectories, and NBA forecasting, alongside scaling experiments, ablations, and density analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical evaluations, revises NBA results, and adds standard deviations for selected evaluations.

M1.justification: The informed random-walk prior, flow-matching objective, spatial and temporal architecture components, Transformer variant, and inference procedure are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A.1–A.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Charged, Springs, and Gravity systems, the same eight MD17 molecules, and the same two NBA forecasting setups. The added variability table uses existing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2–4. NBA setup 1 retains Trajectron++, SVAE, and LaM-SLidE; setup 2 retains GroupNet, LED, and MoFlow. The N-body and MD17 comparisons also retain their original methods.

E3.justification: Reported splits, prediction horizons, metrics, inference budgets, and training configurations remain unchanged. V3 newly specifies ball-target inclusion for the NBA setups, but v2 did not specify this distinction; the addition does not establish an actual protocol revision.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.5 and Table 9 provide a limited analysis of prediction-error variability under different stochastic prior initializations. Existing prior and architecture ablations, scaling analyses, density checks, and trajectory examples are retained.

E5.justification: V3 first reports standard deviations for STFlow on the three N-body systems, seven MD17 molecules, and NBA setup 2. The five or twenty inference samples were already documented in v2. These spreads describe stochastic prediction variability, without establishing additional runs or uncertainty across independent training runs.

E6.justification: Table 4 substantially revises both NBA setups and both STFlow variants. STFlow's Rebound min20ADE/FDE changes from 0.68/1.11 to 0.94/1.55, removing its lead over SVAE's unchanged 0.72/1.37. In setup 2, its mean20 changes from 1.69/2.92 to 1.51/2.59 and min20 from 0.99/1.68 to 1.17/1.94. These are replaced reported results; their cause is unspecified, preventing attribution to a same-setting performance change. Table 9 adds dispersion values, while N-body, MD17, ablation, and existing plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The distribution factorization, coupling and prior definitions, training objective, complexity reasoning, and appendix layer equations are unchanged. No substantive mathematical revision or new proof appears.

C1.justification: The conclusion narrows the quantified error-reduction claim from a range of 16.7%–56.9% to 'up to 56.9%', dropping the asserted lower bound. The central method, efficiency, and scalability contributions remain, as do the broad abstract and introduction performance claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1.3 replaces the claimed NBA setup 1 improvements of 12.9%/20.5% with qualified competitiveness. It newly interprets relatively low mean errors but higher min20 errors as prioritizing fidelity over diversity. The existing limitations and future-work discussion are retained.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-access link in the abstract and documents that NBA setup 1 excludes the ball from the prediction target while setup 2 includes it. Algorithms, hyperparameters, hardware, and runtime disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are retained. Changes to the Yıldız et al. reference concern author rendering and bibliographic metadata for the same work.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the NBA results paragraph, corrects result-table references, updates affiliation and publication text, and inserts a standard-deviations subsection. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 9, repositions Table 5, and relocates or regroups appendix plots under A.6. All twelve existing figures retain their artwork; the changes primarily concern table addition and layout.

improvement.justification: V3 improves reporting transparency through the NBA target clarification, code link, and predictive standard deviations. Its NBA discussion also better reflects the revised Table 4. The gains remain limited: the numerical replacements are unexplained, and the abstract retains a broad lowest-error claim despite the revised NBA rankings.
